en.title: Guilduo permissions: OAuth, Agent scopes and safe writes
en.description: Understand Guilduo OAuth grants and Agent scopes. Diagnose read-only access, distinguish link management from execution, and use previews and conflict checks.
en.lead: Agent execution permissions are the intersection of the OAuth grant and Agent policy. Expanding one side cannot authorize an operation missing from the other.

sections.title: Compare the two permission sets
paragraphs: get_current_agent_context returns connectionScopes, agentAllowedScopes and effectiveExecutionScopes. effectiveScopes is a compatibility field for effective permissions. Read this response to identify which side is missing access.

rows: OAuth scope missing for context inspection

sections.title: Separate linking from execution permissions
paragraphs: get_current_agent_context requires OAuth agents:read. link_agent and unlink_agent use OAuth agents:write to manage this connection's Agent association.
The absence of agents:write from Agent execution scopes alone does not imply link management was lost. Check connectionScopes for connection control and effectiveExecutionScopes for work.
Create, edit and change Agent permissions in the authenticated Web App. Agents and Skills do not automatically expand an OAuth grant.
steps: Missing OAuth scope: the human reviews consent and re-authorizes if needed.
Missing Agent scope: allow only the access needed for its role in the Web App.
Still failing after changes: reread context and verify the intended Agent and effective access.

sections.title: Check preview support and save conditions
bullets: Preview assign_quest_to_agent and request_human_review with dryRun=true; save with the current expectedUpdatedAt.
After previewing transition_quest_handoff, pass expectedState. Do not overwrite from a stale working or other state.
create_quest and update_quest have no dryRun in the published schema. Do not add unsupported inputs; verify the change and existing authorization before executing.
Existing authorization for the same scope does not require repeated approval. Ask for missing decisions or operations outside that scope.

sections.title: Respect human answers and private data
paragraphs: The intended human saves review answers through Web authentication. An Agent cannot mark a confirmation answered with ordinary update or completion tools.
Public profiles contain display name, handle, bio, avatar, level and similar fields. Quest content, notes and authentication data are not public profile fields.
Do not put tokens, API keys, client secrets, model keys or complete UIDs in Quest text, artifact URLs or public reports. Remove credentials and personal data from shared logs.

en.title: Guilduo troubleshooting: connections, scopes and saving
en.description: Diagnose Guilduo 401 errors, unlinked Agents, missing Human tools, write permission failures and Quest conflicts. Recover safely and report useful evidence.
en.lead: First identify whether the failure is endpoint access, OAuth, Agent linking, discovery, permissions or persistence. Inspect the failed read and error before changing connection settings.

sections.title: 401, OAuth callback and account mismatches
paragraphs: A 401 on an unauthenticated protected MCP or REST route can be expected. Opening a URL in a browser alone does not verify a client connection.
steps: Check that the MCP URL is https://mcp.guilduo.com/mcp. https://api.guilduo.com/v1 is the Appwrite API.
Verify that the Web App and OAuth flow use the same account. You may be reading another account's workspace.
Re-authorize OAuth if an old migration-era connection or expired grant is the cause. Do not reuse old grants or tokens.
If OAuth does not return, inspect extensions blocking the callback and the client's return state.

sections.title: Tools or Skills are missing
paragraphs: The /health tool count and actual authenticated client tools are separate checks. Do not expand Agent scopes solely because counts differ.
steps: Identify the required tools. Human Relay needs request_human_review and list_human_requests.
Refresh connection metadata, then restart and begin a new chat if needed.
Check Skill loading separately. An installed Codex companion is not necessarily loaded into an already running conversation.
If Refresh fails, record the client version, exposed tools and error. Do not immediately remove a working connection or create duplicates.

rows: Link the intended Agent and reread context
Allow the necessary scope on the missing side
The human must answer in the Web App

sections.title: 409, retries and uncertain save results
bullets: quest_conflict: reread the Quest and preview with the current expectedUpdatedAt.
Handoff conflict: read the actual state and refresh expectedState. Do not revert accepted work using an old state.
request_key_conflict: different request content reused the same key. Inspect the existing request and use a new key for a new round.
human_request_pending: resume the pending or deferred request. Do not create a duplicate under another key.
Lost save response or 5xx: read the state first. General Quest creation is not made idempotent by a Human request key; decide on a retry after inspecting persistence.

sections.title: Reconnect and report the issue
paragraphs: Previous data can remain read-only during synchronization. Reconnect with the same account and verify saved state. Check Archive after completing a one-off To Do.
Public GitHub Issues are at https://github.com/ELRdn/Guilduo/issues. Include the following to help distinguish authentication, UI and tool-contract issues.
bullets: Client name and version, time, expected behavior and actual result.
Failed tool or REST path, HTTP status and error code.
Whether reading, previewing or saving failed, and the state observed on reread.
A minimal reproduction without credentials or Quest content. Do not publish tokens, complete UIDs or Client IDs.

en.title: Guilduo FAQ: AI execution, storage and approvals
en.description: Answers to common Guilduo questions about Agent execution, archived Quests, Human review, Handoff approval, external integrations, MCP and Workflow Skills.
en.lead: Connected, assigned, started, reviewed and completed are different states. These answers explain the distinctions with examples and practical checks.

sections.title: Does registering an Agent start AI automatically?
paragraphs: No. Agent Registry records a display name, role, instructions and permissions. A connected client such as Codex or Claude supplies the model and work environment.
Setting a Quest to ready does not prove automatic delivery. After delegating Fix the description, read it in the client and verify the working transition and result.
Astra is a companion character, distinct from a registered Agent and the signed-in user. Use the Agents guide to check roles and connections.

sections.title: Why did my completed Quest disappear?
paragraphs: A one-off To Do moves to Archive on completion and leaves Today. Check Archive first; archiving preserves history.
Dailies, Habits and recurring To Dos retain completion history and return for the next occurrence. Completing a child does not automatically complete its parent.
If it is still missing, check All, Backlog, filters and the signed-in account. Follow nextCursor when reading MCP lists.

sections.title: Does a Human answer complete the original Quest?
paragraphs: A Human review response does not automatically complete the original Quest. The response is saved to a separate review Quest; accepting the Handoff and completing the original work are separate explicit actions.
For example, approving the mobile menu does not finish a source Quest that still requires a description change. The Agent must meet the remaining criteria first.
Opening a link, marking it seen or deferring it does not answer the request. The intended human must save an answer through Web authentication.

sections.title: Can Guilduo automatically sync Google Calendar or Notion?
paragraphs: Published documentation marks Provider OAuth for Google Calendar, Google Tasks, Notion and Toggl as preparation. API or tool contracts alone do not establish live connections or automatic synchronization.
Do not send external service keys through an MCP chat. Verify connection state in the Web App and relevant read tools before use.

sections.title: Where can I check paid plan prices and Credits?
paragraphs: These Docs do not publish unapproved plan prices or Credit allowances. Check approved, published sale terms before making a purchase.

These docs cover operations supported by published sources and do not quote unapproved prices, Credit grants, discounts or referral benefits. Base purchase decisions on published, approved sales terms when available.

sections.title: How do MCP, Workflow Skills and plugins differ?
paragraphs: MCP connects tools, a Workflow Skill teaches the operating sequence and a plugin packages Skills or connection configuration. MCP alone does not load a Skill, and a Skill does not grant OAuth permissions.
The local Codex companion can add the Skill to an existing Guilduo App. Local installation is separate from directory publication and official review.

sections.title: Are Guilduo and QuestForge different products?
paragraphs: Guilduo is the current public product name; QuestForge is the legacy name. Technical identifiers in connection settings retain the legacy name for compatibility.
Guilduo is the current product name. questforge MCP IDs, file paths and CLI variables remain for compatibility. Do not rename configuration identifiers merely to match the public name.

en.title: Guilduo API and MCP reference: endpoints and examples
en.description: Use the Guilduo REST API and MCP with canonical endpoints, OAuth, tool schemas and Quest reads. Follow pagination and handle preview and conflict contracts.
en.lead: REST and MCP share the same work rules. Use the published OpenAPI and MCP schemas as references and match inputs to the contract exposed by your connected server.

sections.title: Distinguish REST, MCP and Appwrite
paragraphs: Use /mcp for normal MCP connections. /mcp-next is a validation lane. Do not redirect Worker Quest routes to the Appwrite API.

sections.title: Check authentication and schemas
paragraphs: Ordinary MCP users use OAuth. OpenAPI defines OAuth and Appwrite JWT Bearer authentication. Fixed API-key distribution is not the normal user flow.
api/openapi.json defines REST paths, inputs and responses; api/mcp-tools.json defines tool names and schemas. Check required fields, enums and length limits before calling.
Tool discovery does not replace authentication or Agent policy. Read identity and effective scopes with get_current_agent_context, then read the target's current state.

paragraphs: The following input reads list_quests. Inspect quests, total and nextCursor. If nextCursor is present, pass it as cursor in the next call.
steps: Connect OAuth MCP and verify the intended Agent and required quests:read with get_current_agent_context.
Call list_quests with the input above and compare it with Backlog in the Web App.
Pass an actual returned ID to get_quest as questId and read details and updatedAt. Do not infer IDs from display names.
For REST, use an authenticated GET /v1/quests?view=backlog&kind=todo&limit=5. Do not confuse an unauthenticated 401 with a storage or network failure.

sections.title: Map operations to tools and REST routes
paragraphs: The CLI is a REST client for people and CI. Writes execute when --execute is supplied. CLI usage and OAuth MCP discovery are distinct interfaces.

sections.title: Understand writes and error contracts
bullets: Execute assign_quest_to_agent and request_human_review after preview with the current expectedUpdatedAt. transition_quest_handoff uses expectedState.
Do not add undefined dryRun fields to create_quest or update_quest. Tools with additionalProperties=false reject undefined properties.
For 401 inspect authentication; for 403 permissions and identity; for 409 conflicts. requestKey retries the same Human review round and is not a general Quest-creation retry guarantee.
On conflict, read current state and preview again. Do not repeatedly resend stale timestamps or fabricate a Human answer through general updates.
Tool counts and versions change. Compare the connected tools/list with the published contract and verify compatibility by required names and schemas.
